title: Recurring invoices
plain: Invoices that go out on a schedule. The roadmap says it shipped; it has been switched off in production since late June.
state: Written and merged. It was switched off on 28 June after it created 41 duplicate invoices for one client in a night. A guard against duplicates went in afterwards.
live: Off. The production settings disable it, so no scheduled invoice has gone out since 28 June.
evidence: `config/production.json` disables it, and the comment beside the flag dates the 41 duplicate invoices to 28 June.
from_you: Whether it goes back on now, or stays off until the guard is proven against real data.
remaining: Switching it on is one line. Proving the guard first needs a safe way to replay a real schedule, which is a day.

title: Emailing invoices to clients
plain: Sending an invoice to a client by email. The code is finished and has never had the credential it needs on the live site.
state: Finished and merged. With no sending credential it returns quietly instead of failing, so nothing anywhere reports a problem.
live: Almost certainly not sending. The deploy log records the credential was never set, and its last entry is 4 July — so this is the strongest thing I have, not proof.
evidence: The send path returns quietly when the token is absent, and the deploy log has no entry setting it. That log stops on 4 July, so this is the repository’s account, not the live site’s.
from_you: Confirm whether the credential is set on the live site, and set it if not.
remaining: Nothing in the code. Once it is set, mail sends.

title: The app says “queued” for mail that never left
plain: When email cannot send, the screen still says the invoice is queued, so nobody finds out it did not go.
state: Known, unfixed. It is the reason the missing credential went unnoticed for six weeks.
live: Live, and misleading, on every invoice sent since the first deploy.
remaining: Show the real outcome instead. An hour, and worth doing whatever you decide about the credential.

title: Invoicing in another currency
plain: Billing a client in their own currency. Converting works; rounding the tax and getting live exchange rates do not.
state: Half built. Conversion is done. Tax rounding is unwritten because three defensible rules disagree by cents on every multi-line invoice, and rates need a paid feed.
live: Not live. The feature is switched off in production and two of its three parts do not exist.
evidence: The rounding function throws rather than returning, and the note above it names three rules without choosing one.
from_you: Which rounding rule, and whether to pay for a rate feed or cut this from 1.0.
remaining: Rounding is half a day once the rule is chosen. The feed is an afternoon once it is paid for.

title: Proving the duplicate bug is actually fixed
plain: Showing that the schedule cannot bill the same client twice again, against real data rather than in theory.
state: The guard is written. It has never run against anything but test data, and the call agreed 1.0 does not go out until it has.
live: Nothing to be live — the feature it guards is switched off.
from_you: Only the decision above about when recurring invoices goes back on.
remaining: A replay of one real schedule against a copy of the data. A day, once you have said which way round it goes.

title: A portal where clients see their own invoices
plain: Clients get a link, see everything you have billed them, and pay from there. Nothing for this exists yet.
state: An idea from the call on 11 August. No design, no code, not on the roadmap.
from_you: Whether this is part of 1.0, comes after it, or is dropped.
remaining: Weeks rather than days — it needs client accounts, a payment step and a public surface to defend.

title: Chasing invoices that are overdue
plain: An automatic nudge at seven, fourteen and thirty days. Small, and it can only work once email does.
state: An idea from the call. Not started, and it rests entirely on email working in production.
remaining: Two days, and it cannot be trusted before the email credential is sorted.

title: The seven features that are genuinely done
plain: Creating and sending invoices, clients, PDF export, payment tracking, dashboard totals, tax lines and importing past invoices.
state: Built, merged, and running in production. 191 tests pass.
evidence: Each of the seven appears in the deploy log with a date, and none carries a disabling flag in the production settings. Nothing here was exercised against the running site.
